title: Weights, biases and total of a three-layer MLP
prompt: An MLP for flattened 28×28 grayscale images has the layers 784 → 256 → 128 → 10. Every Linear layer has a bias, and the activations (ReLU) have no parameters. Count the weights, the biases and the total number of trainable parameters.
hints: A Linear(i, o) layer has an o × i weight matrix and o biases.
Add the three layers separately before summing.
explanation:
Weights: 784·256 = 200,704, 256·128 = 32,768, 128·10 = 1,280, so 234,752 weights.

Biases: 256 + 128 + 10 = 394.

Total = 234,752 + 394 = 235,146. Forgetting the biases gives 234,752; counting the 784 input pixels as extra parameters would be wrong because inputs are not learned.

title: Bias-free MLP on flattened colour images
prompt: Input images have shape (N, 3, 32, 32). The model is Flatten → Linear(3072, 512, bias=False) → ReLU → Linear(512, 512, bias=False) → ReLU → Linear(512, 10, bias=False). How many trainable parameters does it have?
hints: Flatten and ReLU have no parameters.
Without bias a Linear layer has in·out parameters.
explanation: 3072·512 = 1,572,864; 512·512 = 262,144; 512·10 = 5,120. Total = 1,840,128. The batch size N and the spatial size do not matter because the flattened vector length 3·32·32 = 3072 is already given.

title: A 7×7 strided convolution stem
prompt: A ResNet-style stem is nn.Conv2d(3, 64, kernel_size=7, stride=2, padding=3, bias=False) followed by nn.BatchNorm2d(64) and a ReLU. How many trainable parameters does the convolution alone have, and how many does the convolution plus BatchNorm have?
hints: Stride and padding change the output size, not the number of weights.
BatchNorm2d(C) with affine=True has a scale and a shift per channel.
explanation: The filter bank has 64 filters of size 3×7×7: 64·3·7·7 = 9,408 weights, and there is no bias. BatchNorm2d(64) adds γ and β for each of the 64 channels: 2·64 = 128. Total with BN = 9,536. The running mean and variance are buffers, not trainable parameters.

title: Convolution with a rectangular kernel
prompt: Count the trainable parameters of nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=(3, 5), bias=True).
hints: The kernel height and width multiply independently.
explanation: Each of the 32 filters has 16·3·5 = 240 weights, giving 32·240 = 7,680 weights, plus 32 biases: 7,712.

title: Factorizing a 7×7 convolution
prompt: Inception-style networks replace a k×k convolution by a 1×k convolution followed by a k×1 convolution. Both layers map 64 → 64 channels, have no bias and use groups = 1. Compare the number of weights of one 7×7 convolution with the factorized pair (1×7 then 7×1).
hints: Count each layer as out · in · kh · kw.
The factorized pair has two layers of 64·64·7 weights.
explanation:
7×7: 64·64·49 = 200,704.

1×7: 64·64·7 = 28,672; 7×1: also 28,672; together 57,344.

The pair has 2·7 = 14 weights per channel pair instead of 49, a reduction of about 3.50× (ratio 49/14 = 3.5), while covering the same 7×7 receptive field.

title: Grouped 3×3 convolution versus standard
prompt: Count the trainable parameters of nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, groups=4, bias=True), and of the standard convolution nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, bias=True) with the same sizes.
hints: With g groups each filter only sees Cin/g input channels.
The bias count does not depend on the groups.
explanation:
Grouped: each filter has (32/4)·3·3 = 72 weights, so 64·72 = 4,608 weights + 64 biases = 4,672.

Standard: 64·32·9 = 18,432 weights + 64 biases = 18,496.

The weights shrink by the factor g = 4, the biases do not.

title: Depthwise-separable convolution
prompt: A depthwise-separable layer maps 64 → 128 channels with a 3×3 depthwise convolution (groups = 64, 64 → 64 channels) followed by a 1×1 pointwise convolution (64 → 128). There are no biases. Count the weights of each part and in total, and compare with one standard 3×3 convolution from 64 to 128 channels.
hints: Depthwise: one 3×3 filter per channel.
Pointwise: every output channel mixes all 64 input channels.
explanation:
Depthwise: 64 filters of 1·3·3 = 9 weights: 576.

Pointwise: 128·64·1·1 = 8,192.

Total: 576 + 8,192 = 8,768.

Standard: 128·64·9 = 73,728, which is about 8.4× more. The general ratio is 1/Cout + 1/9 = 0.119.

title: A Network-in-Network mlpconv block
prompt: An mlpconv block is a k×k convolution followed by two 1×1 convolutions: Conv2d(3, 192, 5), Conv2d(192, 160, 1), Conv2d(160, 96, 1). All have bias=True and groups=1; ReLUs have no parameters. How many trainable parameters does the block have?
hints: A 1×1 convolution is a Linear layer applied at every pixel.

title: Parameters of a 2× upsampling transposed convolution
prompt: A decoder uses nn.ConvTranspose2d(64, 32, kernel_size=4, stride=2, padding=1, bias=True) for 2× upsampling. How many trainable parameters does it have?
hints: PyTorch stores the weight as Cin × (Cout/groups) × kh × kw.
Stride and padding do not change the parameter count.
explanation: Weight shape (64, 32, 4, 4): 64·32·16 = 32,768. Plus 32 biases: 32,800. Stride 2 and padding 1 only determine the output size.

title: Grouped transposed convolution
prompt: Count the weights of nn.ConvTranspose2d(32, 48, kernel_size=3, groups=8, bias=False) and of the same layer with groups=1.
hints: ConvTranspose2d stores weight shape (Cin, Cout/groups, kh, kw).
Each group maps Cin/g input channels to Cout/g output channels.
explanation:
groups = 8: shape (32, 48/8, 3, 3) = (32, 6, 3, 3): 32·6·9 = 1,728. Equivalently 8 groups × (4 in × 6 out × 9).

groups = 1: shape (32, 48, 3, 3): 32·48·9 = 13,824. The grouped layer has g = 8 times fewer weights.

title: BatchNorm: trainable parameters versus buffers
prompt: For nn.BatchNorm2d(96) with default settings (affine=True, track_running_stats=True), give the number of trainable scalar parameters, the number of scalars in the running statistics (running_mean and running_var), and the total number of scalars in the whole state_dict (including the one-element num_batches_tracked).
hints: γ and β are learned by gradient descent; running statistics are updated by the moving average.
state_dict contains weight, bias, running_mean, running_var and num_batches_tracked.
explanation:
Trainable: γ (weight) and β (bias), each of length 96: 2·96 = 192.

Buffers: running_mean (96) + running_var (96) = 192 values; they are not touched by the optimizer.

state_dict: weight 96 + bias 96 + running_mean 96 + running_var 96 + num_batches_tracked 1 = 385 scalars.

title: Two convolutions with different BatchNorm settings
prompt: Input channels: 3. Count all trainable parameters of the model and, separately, the trainable parameters of the two BatchNorm layers.
code:
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1, bias=True),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(64, affine=False), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Conv2d(64, 64, 3, padding=1, bias=True),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(),
)

parts.label: Trainable parameters of the BatchNorm layers

hints: affine=False removes γ and β.
Both convolutions use a bias.
explanation:
Conv1: 64·3·9 + 64 = 1,792. Conv2: 64·64·9 + 64 = 36,928. BatchNorm2d(64, affine=False) has no trainable parameters; BatchNorm2d(64) has γ and β: 128.

Total = 1,792 + 36,928 + 128 = 38,848.

title: Folding BatchNorm into a convolution for inference
prompt: During training a block is Conv2d(64, 128, 3, bias=False) followed by BatchNorm2d(128). For deployment, BatchNorm is folded into the convolution, giving a single Conv2d(64, 128, 3) that needs a bias. How many parameters does the training-time block have, and how many does the folded convolution have?
hints: The folded weights are the old weights rescaled per output channel.
The BN shift becomes the new bias.
explanation:
Training: 128·64·9 = 73,728 conv weights + 2·128 = 256 BN parameters = 73,984.

Fused: the weights keep their shape (73,728), γ/√(σ²+ε) is absorbed into them, and β − γμ/√(σ²+ε) becomes a bias of length 128: 73,856. Folding removes the 128 extra parameters.

title: Parameters of LayerNorm variants
prompt: Give the number of trainable parameters of (a) nn.LayerNorm([64, 28, 28]) with elementwise_affine=True, (b) nn.LayerNorm(768), and (c) nn.LayerNorm(768, bias=False).
hints: The affine parameters have the shape of normalized_shape.
bias=False drops only the shift β.
explanation:
(a) γ and β both have shape (64, 28, 28): 2·64·784 = 100,352. This is the image-style layer norm over all of C, H, W.

(b) 2·768 = 1,536.

(c) only γ remains: 768.

title: GroupNorm, InstanceNorm and the number of groups
prompt: The feature map has C = 256 channels. How many trainable parameters do nn.GroupNorm(32, 256), nn.GroupNorm(1, 256), the default nn.InstanceNorm2d(256) and nn.InstanceNorm2d(256, affine=True) have?
hints: GroupNorm learns a scale and shift per channel, not per group.
InstanceNorm2d has affine=False by default.
explanation: GroupNorm always has γ, β of length C = 256, independent of the number of groups: 2·256 = 512 (both for G = 32 and G = 1). InstanceNorm2d defaults to affine=False, so it has 0 trainable parameters; with affine=True it is again 2·256 = 512.

title: RMSNorm parameters in a decoder-only model
prompt: A language model uses RMSNorm with only a learned scale γ of length D = 4096 (no shift). Each of its 32 transformer blocks has two RMSNorm layers (before attention and before the MLP), and there is one final RMSNorm before the output layer. How many parameters does one RMSNorm have and how many do all RMSNorm layers have together?
hints: No mean subtraction and no β: only γ remains.
Count the norm layers first: 2 per block plus the final one.
explanation: One RMSNorm: γ ∈ R^4096, so 4096 parameters. Number of layers: 2·32 + 1 = 65. Total = 65·4096 = 266,240.

title: Token and position embeddings with a tied head
prompt: A tiny language model has a vocabulary of 32,000 tokens, width D = 512 and a maximum sequence length of 256. It uses nn.Embedding(32000, 512) for tokens and a learned nn.Embedding(256, 512) for positions. The output layer is Linear(512, 32000, bias=False). Give the token-embedding parameters, the position-embedding parameters, and the total of the three if the output weights are untied, and the total if they are tied to the token embedding.
hints: An embedding table is a vocab × D matrix.
Tying means the output layer reuses the same matrix, adding no new parameters.

title: Multi-head attention projections
prompt: A multi-head self-attention layer has width D = 512 and h = 8 heads (d_head = 64). It has four projections $W_Q$, $W_K$, $W_V$, $W_O$, each D × D. Count the parameters of one projection with bias, all four with bias, and all four without bias.
hints: The number of heads only splits D into h pieces; it does not add parameters.
Each projection has D outputs, so D biases.
explanation: One projection: 512·512 + 512 = 262,656. Four projections: 4·262,656 = 1,050,624. Without bias: 4·512² = 1,048,576. Using h = 1 or h = 16 would give exactly the same numbers.

title: nn.MultiheadAttention parameter count
prompt: Count the trainable parameters of nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim=256, num_heads=4) with default settings (bias=True). It stores one packed in_proj_weight of shape (3·256, 256), an in_proj_bias, and an out_proj Linear(256, 256). Give the size of in_proj_weight and the total.
hints: The packed in_proj is Q, K and V stacked.
Remember in_proj_bias and out_proj.bias.

title: Cross-attention with different input widths
prompt: In a cross-attention layer the queries come from decoder vectors of width 256, while keys and values come from encoder vectors of width 128. There are 4 heads of size 32, so queries, keys and values all have width 4·32 = 128, and the output projection maps back to 256. There are no biases. Give the number of weights in $W_Q$, $W_K$ and the total of $W_Q$, $W_K$, $W_V$, $W_O$.
hints: The shape of each matrix is (input width × output width).
W_O maps the concatenated heads (128) back to the decoder width (256).
explanation: W_Q: 256·128 = 32,768. W_K: 128·128 = 16,384. W_V: 128·128 = 16,384. W_O: 128·256 = 32,768. Total = 98,304. The encoder length and decoder length never appear in a parameter count.

title: Grouped-query attention
prompt: A layer with D = 1024 uses 16 query heads of size 64, but only 4 key/value heads of size 64 shared across groups of query heads (grouped-query attention). No biases. Count the weights of $W_K$ and the total of $W_Q$, $W_K$, $W_V$, $W_O$, and compare with standard multi-head attention with 16 key/value heads.
hints: The key/value width is (number of KV heads) · d_head.
W_Q and W_O still map to and from 16·64 = 1024.

title: Transformer MLP block
prompt: The MLP of a transformer block with D = 768 is Linear(768, 3072) → GELU → Linear(3072, 768), both with bias. How many trainable parameters does it have?
hints: The hidden width is 4D.

title: SwiGLU versus ReLU MLP
prompt: A gated MLP (SwiGLU) with D = 512 has three bias-free matrices: gate and up projections 512 → 1408 and a down projection 1408 → 512. A standard bias-free MLP uses 512 → 2048 → 512. Give the number of parameters of both.
hints: SwiGLU has three weight matrices, the standard MLP two.
The hidden width of the gated version is chosen near 8D/3 to match the budget.

title: Parameters of one transformer encoder block
prompt: One encoder block has width D = 384, 6 attention heads, an MLP with hidden width 4D, and two LayerNorms (each with γ and β). All Linear layers, including the four attention projections, have a bias. Give the parameters of the attention sub-layer, the MLP, the two LayerNorms and the whole block.
hints: Attention is four D × D projections with bias.
Each LayerNorm has 2D parameters.

title: ViT patch embedding, class token and position table
prompt: A ViT-Base front end processes 3×224×224 images. The patch embedding is Conv2d(3, 768, kernel_size=16, stride=16) with bias. It adds one learned class token (a vector of length 768) and a learned position embedding with one row per token (196 patches + 1 class token) of width 768. Give the parameters of the patch embedding and the total of all three components.

parts.label: Total of conv + class token + position table

hints: The number of patches is (224/16)² = 196.
The position table has 197 rows.

title: Total parameters of a tiny Vision Transformer
prompt: A tiny ViT classifies 3×32×32 images. Patch embedding: Conv2d(3, 64, kernel_size=4, stride=4) with bias (64 patches). A learned class token (64) and learned position embedding for 65 tokens (65×64) are added. There are 2 pre-norm encoder blocks (width 64, 4 heads, MLP hidden width 256, two LayerNorms per block with γ and β, all Linear layers with bias), then a final LayerNorm(64) and a classification head Linear(64, 10) with bias. How many trainable parameters does the model have in total?
hints: Compute one block first and multiply by 2.
Do not forget the class token, position table and final LayerNorm.

title: ResNet basic block that downsamples
prompt: A downsampling ResNet basic block has the main path Conv3×3(64 → 128, stride 2) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(128 → 128) – BN, and a shortcut Conv1×1(64 → 128, stride 2) – BN. All convolutions are bias-free. Count the trainable parameters of the main path, the shortcut and the whole block.
hints: Strides do not change the parameter counts.
Each BatchNorm2d(128) has 256 trainable parameters.

title: Bottleneck block with projection shortcut
prompt: A ResNet bottleneck block receives 256 channels and produces 512. Main path: Conv1×1(256 → 128) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(128 → 128) – BN – ReLU – Conv1×1(128 → 512) – BN. Shortcut: Conv1×1(256 → 512) – BN. All convolutions are bias-free. Count the parameters of the main path (convolutions and BNs), of the shortcut and the whole block.
hints: Count conv weights and BN parameters separately.
BN2d(C) has 2C trainable parameters.

title: ResNeXt block with a grouped 3×3 convolution
prompt: A ResNeXt bottleneck with identity shortcut has Conv1×1(256 → 128) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(128 → 128, groups=32) – BN – ReLU – Conv1×1(128 → 256) – BN. All convolutions are bias-free. How many weights does the grouped 3×3 convolution have, and how many trainable parameters (convolutions + BN) does the block have?
hints: Each group sees 128/32 = 4 input channels and produces 4 output channels.
BN follows each of the three convolutions.

title: U-Net double-convolution block
prompt: The standard U-Net encoder block is Conv3×3(32 → 64, padding 1, bias=False) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(64 → 64, padding 1, bias=False) – BN – ReLU. How many trainable parameters does it have?
hints: Padding does not change parameter counts.
Two BatchNorm2d(64) layers add 128 parameters each.

title: U-Net decoder up-step with skip concatenation
prompt: A decoder step receives 256 channels, applies ConvTranspose2d(256, 128, kernel_size=2, stride=2) with bias, concatenates the result with a 128-channel skip feature (giving 256 channels), and applies Conv3×3(256 → 128) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(128 → 128) – BN – ReLU with bias-free convolutions. Count the parameters of the up-convolution, of the convolution block (including BNs) and of the whole step.
hints: The first 3×3 convolution sees the concatenated 256 channels.
The skip connection itself has no parameters.

title: Pixel shuffle versus transposed convolution
prompt: Two ways to upsample a 64-channel feature map by 2× while producing 24 channels. (a) Conv2d(64, 24·2², kernel_size=3, padding=1) with bias followed by PixelShuffle(2). (b) ConvTranspose2d(64, 24, kernel_size=2, stride=2) with bias. Give the number of parameters of both.
hints: PixelShuffle rearranges values and has no parameters.
The convolution in (a) must output C'·r² = 96 channels.
explanation:
(a) The conv has 24·4 = 96 output channels: 96·64·9 + 96 = 55,296 + 96 = 55,392; PixelShuffle adds 0.

(b) 64·24·2·2 + 24 = 6,144 + 24 = 6,168.

The 3×3 conv at low resolution is about 9.0× larger in parameters.

title: Squeeze-and-Excitation block
prompt: A squeeze-and-excitation block on C = 256 channels with reduction ratio 16 computes s = σ(W₂ ReLU(W₁ z)) from the pooled vector z. W₁ is Linear(256, 16) and W₂ is Linear(16, 256), both with bias. The global average pooling has no parameters. How many trainable parameters does the block have?
hints: Two small Linear layers, one narrowing and one widening.

title: Inverted residual (MBConv) block
prompt: An inverted bottleneck maps 24 → 32 channels with expansion ratio 6: Conv1×1(24 → 144) – BN – ReLU6 – depthwise Conv3×3(144 channels, groups=144) – BN – ReLU6 – Conv1×1(144 → 32) – BN. All convolutions are bias-free. Count the trainable parameters (convolutions and BNs).
hints: The expanded width is 6·24 = 144.
The depthwise convolution has one 3×3 filter per channel.

title: Layers of a DenseNet-B dense block
prompt: A dense block has growth rate k = 32 and block input of 64 channels. Layer ℓ receives all earlier features concatenated (64, 96 and 128 channels for layers 1, 2 and 3) and applies BN – ReLU – Conv1×1(→ 4k = 128) – BN – ReLU – Conv3×3(128 → 32), with bias-free convolutions. Count the trainable parameters of layer 1, of layer 3 and of the whole 3-layer block.
hints: Only the first BN and the 1×1 convolution depend on the input channel count.
The 3×3 convolution always maps 128 → 32.

title: Inception module with 1×1 reductions
prompt: An Inception module receives 192 channels. Branch 1: Conv1×1(192 → 64). Branch 2: Conv1×1(192 → 96) then Conv3×3(96 → 128). Branch 3: Conv1×1(192 → 16) then Conv5×5(16 → 32). Branch 4: 3×3 max-pooling, then Conv1×1(192 → 32). All convolutions have a bias and groups = 1. Give the parameters of branch 2 and of the whole module.
hints: Max-pooling has no parameters.
Each convolution has out·in·kh·kw weights plus out biases.

title: The fully connected head of a VGG-style network
prompt: The classifier head of VGG-16 flattens a 512×7×7 tensor (25,088 values) and applies Linear(25088, 4096) – ReLU – Linear(4096, 4096) – ReLU – Linear(4096, 1000), all with bias. The first layer can be rewritten as Conv2d(512, 4096, kernel_size=7). Give the parameters of that convolution and of the whole head.
hints: The 7×7 convolution has exactly one weight for every input value of the flattened vector.
Add the three Linear layers.

title: LeNet-style network: flatten size and total
prompt: Input shape (N, 1, 32, 32). Conv2d(1, 6, 5) – ReLU – MaxPool2d(2) – Conv2d(6, 16, 5) – ReLU – MaxPool2d(2) – Flatten – Linear(____, 120) – ReLU – Linear(120, 84) – ReLU – Linear(84, 10). Convolutions use stride 1 and no padding; all layers have bias. Find the missing in_features and the total number of trainable parameters.
code:
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(1, 6, 5), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Conv2d(6, 16, 5), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(____, 120), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(120, 84), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(84, 10),
)
hints: Track the spatial size: 32 → 28 → 14 → 10 → 5.
Pooling has no parameters.

title: Shape tracking with stride and dilation, then counting
prompt: Input shape (N, 3, 64, 64). Use floor rounding for output sizes. Find the missing in_features of the Linear layer and the total number of trainable parameters. All convolutions and the Linear layer have a bias; BatchNorm2d has affine=True.
code:
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(3, 16, 5, stride=2, padding=2), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1, dilation=2), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(____, 10),
)
hints: Use H_out = floor((H + 2p − d(k−1) − 1)/s) + 1 for convolution and pooling.
The dilated 3×3 convolution acts like a 5×5 kernel.

title: Trainable parameters when the backbone is frozen
prompt: A frozen pretrained backbone (all parameters have requires_grad=False) outputs 2048-dimensional features. On top, a new head is trained: Linear(2048, 512) – BatchNorm1d(512) – ReLU – Linear(512, 20), with bias. How many parameters will the optimizer update?
hints: Frozen parameters are excluded.
BatchNorm1d(512) has γ and β but its running statistics are buffers.
explanation: Linear 1: 2048·512 + 512 = 1,049,088. BatchNorm1d: 2·512 = 1,024. Linear 2: 512·20 + 20 = 10,260. Total = 1,060,372. The running mean and variance (1,024 values) are not parameters.

title: A 1D convolutional audio front end
prompt: A raw-waveform front end is Conv1d(1, 64, kernel_size=10, stride=5) with bias, Conv1d(64, 80, kernel_size=3) with bias, and a depthwise Conv1d(80, 80, kernel_size=3, groups=80) without bias. Count the parameters of each layer and the total.
hints: A 1D convolution has out·in·k weights.
The depthwise layer has one length-3 filter per channel.

title: Weight sharing in a Siamese network
prompt: A Siamese network applies the same encoder Linear(100, 64) – ReLU – Linear(64, 16) (with bias) to two inputs, concatenates the two 16-dimensional embeddings and feeds the 32-dimensional vector to Linear(32, 1) with bias. Count the trainable parameters of the model with the shared encoder, and of a variant with two separate encoders.
hints: Shared weights are counted once.
The head sees 2·16 = 32 inputs.

title: Autoencoder with tied weights
prompt: An autoencoder encodes with $h = \text{ReLU}(Wx + b_1)$, $W \in \mathbb{R}^{128\times 784}$, and decodes with $\hat{x} = W^\top h + b_2$ using the transpose of the same matrix. Count the trainable parameters with tied weights, and with an untied decoder matrix of its own.
hints: Tied: the transposed matrix is the same 128·784 numbers.
Each layer still has its own bias.
explanation:
Tied: W has 128·784 = 100,352 entries, b₁ has 128 and b₂ has 784: 101,264.

Untied: encoder 100,480 + decoder 128·784 + 784 = 101,136: 201,616.
